overview: FactSet is a global provider of integrated financial data, analytics, and workflow software for the investment community, delivering content through its flagship Workstation, data feeds/APIs, portfolio analytics, and enterprise solutions. Founded in 1978 and headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut, the subscription-based business serves roughly 9,000+ client firms and 230,000+ individual professional users spanning institutional asset managers, hedge funds, wealth managers, banks, corporates, and private equity/venture capital, with buy-side clients far outweighing sell-side. Revenue is roughly two-thirds Americas with the balance split between EMEA and Asia Pacific, and the company operates on an August 31 fiscal year-end.

business_model.summary: FactSet sells forward-looking, recurring subscriptions measured internally as Annual Subscription Value (ASV) — the next-12-months run-rate of all subscription services currently supplied to clients — rather than reporting product-line revenue splits publicly. Growth is driven by a mix of price increases, upsells to existing clients (the primary driver), new client wins, and, to a lesser extent, acquisitions net of attrition. Gross/annual ASV retention has stayed above 95%, and organic ASV growth re-accelerated through FY2026 (ending at roughly 7% in Q4) after a softer FY2025, a trend management attributes partly to AI-related product adoption (AI solutions ASV added in FY2026 more than doubled year over year). Average client tenure exceeds 16 years, with nine of the top 10 clients (by ASV) having been with FactSet for more than two decades, reflecting extremely high revenue durability once a client is onboarded. FY2026 results showed top-line strength (revenue +6.7% to $2.48B, organic ASV growth near the high end of guidance) alongside margin pressure: GAAP operating margin fell roughly 390bps to ~28.3% on $46.2M of restructuring/severance charges tied to a global workforce reduction (headcount down ~2.8% to ~12,444) and continued AI/strategic investment spend, plus ongoing remediation costs tied to a disclosed IT general-controls material weakness.

revenue_streams.name: Workstation/Research (desktop analytics, data, and workflow platform)
Analytics & Trading / Content & Technology Solutions (CTS) — enterprise data feeds, managed services, real-time market data (expanded via BCC Group acquisition)
Other (Irwin IR/capital markets platform, LiquidityBook OMS/trading, Real Estate solutions, LogoIntern)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/enterprise subscriptions — institutional asset managers, hedge funds, wealth managers, banks/sell-side, asset owners, corporates, and private equity/VC firms; contracts increasingly structured as multi-year enterprise agreements with extended average terms rather than single-seat licenses
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~65%, EMEA ~25%, Asia Pacific ~10% of total revenue (FY2026)

main_competitors: Numerous fintech/AI-native data and analytics startups (e.g., Finster AI, generative research copilots)
competitive_position.market_position: A top-tier but not dominant player in the financial data/analytics terminal market; industry estimates put Bloomberg at roughly one-third market share, Refinitiv/LSEG around 20%, S&P Capital IQ around 6%, and FactSet around 4-5%, with FactSet punching above that share in portfolio analytics, buy-side workflow, and increasingly wealth management, IR/capital markets (via Irwin), trading/OMS (via LiquidityBook), and real-time market data (via the BCC Group acquisition, announced September 2026).

moat_factors.description: Client relationships average 16+ years with 95%+ ASV retention; workflows, custom analytics, and integrations become deeply embedded in client operations, making rip-and-replace costly and risky for institutional users.

Proprietary aggregation and normalization of fundamental, estimates, ownership, fixed income, and alternative datasets across thousands of sources, combined with portfolio analytics tools, creates a defensible integrated offering that is hard to replicate piecemeal.

CTS/data feed and API business embeds FactSet data directly into client-built systems and now into third-party AI platforms (Google Gemini via a June 2026 partnership, Anthropic Claude via Cowork), extending the moat beyond the desktop Workstation and creating a defensible role as a trusted, auditable data layer for AI agents in regulated finance.

moat_factors.factor: Brand and reputation for data quality/compliance
moat_factors.description: Decades-long reputation for accuracy and audit trails in a highly regulated industry, valuable as AI agent outputs increasingly require sourced, defensible data — though an unresolved IT general-controls material weakness (open since FY2024, still disclosed as of the FY2026 10-K) is a reputational and execution blemish on this exact strength.

Large fixed cost base in data licensing, content operations (including offshore data operations in India and the Philippines), and R&D is spread across a large global client base, though this scale advantage is smaller than Bloomberg's or LSEG's.

weaknesses: Smaller scale than Bloomberg and LSEG/Refinitiv, limiting negotiating leverage with data suppliers and constraining pricing power in head-to-head competitive takeaways
Sell-side ASV (~18% of book) is more cyclical and tied to investment banking headcount/budgets, which have been volatile

Perceived vulnerability to AI/LLM-based tools that could commoditize basic data retrieval and analysis, compressing the value of legacy workstation seats — the dominant bear narrative that cut the stock roughly in half from its 2025 highs before a partial recovery through late 2026
Historically modest revenue growth (mid-single-digit-to-7% ASV growth) relative to software peers, making the stock reliant on margin expansion and buybacks for EPS growth

Unresolved IT general-controls material weakness (change management, user access, segregation of duties) first disclosed in FY2024 and still open through the FY2026 10-K, creating financial-reporting risk and headline risk

Leadership turnover in 2025-2026 (new CEO Sanoke Viswanathan since September 2025; CFO Helen Shan replaced by Joshua Warren effective April 2026; reported turnover in the Chief People Officer role as well) adds execution/transition risk during a period of heavy AI investment and restructuring

growth_drivers: AI product adoption inside the FactSet platform: clients using FactSet AI solutions are growing ASV materially faster than the rest of the client base, and AI solutions ASV added in FY2026 more than doubled year over year

Strategic partnership with Google Cloud (announced June 2026) embedding Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform capabilities into the Workstation and building jointly developed agents for portfolio operations, deal advisory, and corporate finance

Distribution of FactSet data into third-party AI ecosystems, including a connector enabling FactSet market data inside Anthropic's Claude (via Cowork, February 2026) and an investment/partnership with Finster AI (March 2026) for AI-native banking workflows, positioning FactSet as a trusted, auditable data layer for AI agents rather than being purely disintermediated by them

Continued upsell/cross-sell into the existing client base, historically the primary driver of ASV growth (more impactful than new logo wins), reinforced by enterprise contracts with extended average terms and no price compression

Bolt-on M&A expanding adjacent categories: BCC Group International (real-time market data infrastructure, announced September 2026), LiquidityBook (trading/OMS, closed Feb 2025), Irwin (IR/capital markets platform, closed Nov 2024), and LogoIntern (junior-banker tools)
Wealth management vertical expansion, including a TIFIN.AI partnership (2026) layering agentic workflow technology onto FactSet market data and analytics for wealth managers

Medium-term financial algorithm laid out at the November 10, 2026 Investor Day: targeting ~6% compounded organic revenue growth, adjusted operating margin of 36%+ and ~10% compounded adjusted EPS growth through FY2029, implying margin recovery once restructuring and remediation costs roll off
International/Asia-Pacific expansion, still FactSet's smallest region (~10% of revenue) and a longer-runway growth opportunity

business.risk: AI/LLM disruption of the terminal/workflow model
business.description: Generative AI tools threaten to commoditize basic financial data retrieval and analysis that historically justified premium workstation seat pricing. This remains the single largest overhang on the stock and the primary driver of FactSet's sharp 2026 drawdown; the bear case argues AI could shrink seat counts even as FactSet embeds AI into its own product.

business.risk: Intense competition from larger, better-capitalized rivals
business.description: Bloomberg (~33% share) and LSEG/Refinitiv (~20% share) dominate the market; both have greater scale, data breadth, and resources to invest in competing AI capabilities, potentially pressuring FactSet's pricing and win rates.
The ~18% of ASV tied to sell-side/banking clients is more sensitive to capital markets activity, M&A volumes, and bank headcount than the stickier buy-side book.

business.risk: Workforce reduction and leadership turnover execution risk
business.description: FactSet cut global headcount by ~2.8% in FY2026 ($46.2M restructuring/severance charges) while simultaneously transitioning CEO (Sept 2025) and CFO (April 2026); concurrent cost-cutting, AI investment and leadership change raises execution risk.

LiquidityBook, Irwin, and the newly announced BCC Group acquisition represent a more acquisitive posture than FactSet's historically organic growth model; successful integration across trading/OMS, IR, and real-time market data is not guaranteed.

financial.description: Debt-funded acquisitions (LiquidityBook, Irwin, BCC Group) have increased leverage from FactSet's historically conservative balance sheet, though interest coverage remains healthy and free cash flow grew 14.6% to $707.5M in FY2026.
With roughly a third of revenue generated outside the Americas, USD strength/weakness affects reported (though not organic) ASV and revenue growth.

financial.risk: Margin compression from restructuring and AI investment
financial.description: GAAP operating margin fell ~390bps to ~28.3% in FY2026 on restructuring/severance charges and continued strategic (AI) investment; FY2027 adjusted operating margin guidance of 34.75-35.25% still implies only gradual margin recovery, with the 36%+ target pushed out to FY2029.

financial.risk: IT general-controls material weakness / financial reporting risk
financial.description: FactSet has disclosed an unremediated material weakness in IT general controls (change management, user access, segregation of duties) since FY2024, still open as of recent 10-Q/10-K filings; remediation costs and the risk of a reporting error are an ongoing overhang.

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and cross-border data regulation
regulatory.description: As a global aggregator of financial and personal data (including in wealth management), FactSet is subject to evolving data privacy regimes (GDPR and similar) across the jurisdictions it operates in.

Emerging AI regulation could affect how FactSet and its partners (Google, Anthropic, Finster AI, TIFIN.AI) can deploy AI agents using licensed/proprietary financial data, particularly around explainability and auditability requirements in regulated finance.

macro.risk: Capital markets and asset management industry sensitivity
macro.description: Demand from FactSet's core client base (asset managers, banks, hedge funds) is correlated with AUM levels, trading volumes, and financial industry headcount, all sensitive to equity market performance and economic cycles.

macro.risk: Cost-cutting pressure on financial industry clients
macro.description: In weak economic conditions, buy-side and sell-side clients scrutinize data/research spend and may consolidate vendors or seek lower-cost alternatives, pressuring ASV growth and seat counts.
Higher rates raise the cost of debt-funded M&A and can pressure asset manager profitability/spending indirectly, though FactSet's own recurring subscription model is not highly rate-sensitive.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global financial data and analytics market is large (multi-tens of billions of dollars) and growing at a mid-single-digit rate, with AI integration the dominant strategic theme reshaping competitive dynamics — both a cost/efficiency opportunity for incumbents like FactSet and an existential-threat narrative that drove significant investor skepticism (and a sharp drawdown) earlier in 2026, before partially reversing into year-end on Q4 results and the November Investor Day.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Subscription-based, high-retention revenue provides resilience, but ASV growth, new client wins, and especially sell-side demand correlate with financial industry health, AUM growth, and capital markets activity.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate direct sensitivity (recurring subscription revenue); moderate indirect sensitivity via financial-industry client budgets and the cost of debt used for acquisitions.
key_input_costs: Technology/cloud infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure)
Skilled labor (engineering, content operations, including offshore centers in India and the Philippines)
AI/LLM compute costs for embedded AI features
Restructuring/severance costs tied to the FY2026 workforce reduction

recent_developments.event: Hosted Investor Day 2026, laying out a medium-term financial algorithm through fiscal 2029 (targeting ~6% compounded organic revenue growth, 36%+ adjusted operating margin, ~10% compounded adjusted EPS growth, 90%+ free cash flow conversion) and reaffirming FY2027 guidance (organic ASV growth 5.0-6.5%, revenue $2,600-2,625M, adjusted operating margin 34.75-35.25%, adjusted diluted EPS $19.25-19.65).

Board declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $1.16/share, payable December 17, 2026 to holders of record as of November 30, 2026; shares traded near $332, within ~5% of the 52-week high of $348 and well above the 52-week low of $185 reached earlier in the year.

Reported Q4/FY2026 results: Q4 revenue of $634.7M (+6.3% YoY, organic +7.1%) and adjusted EPS of $4.52 (+11.6% YoY), both beating consensus (~$628M revenue, ~$4.32 EPS). Full-year revenue rose 6.7% to $2.48B and adjusted diluted EPS rose 6.1% to $18.01; free cash flow grew 14.6% to $707.5M. GAAP operating margin fell ~390bps to ~28.3% and GAAP net income fell ~21% on $46.2M of restructuring/severance charges tied to a global workforce reduction (headcount down ~2.8% to ~12,444). AI solutions ASV added in FY2026 more than doubled YoY. Stock reaction was mixed: a clean headline beat was tempered by a softer-than-hoped FY2027 subscription growth guide.

Announced acquisition of BCC Group International GmbH (bccg), a German real-time market data/software firm, folding its ONE Platform into FactSet's Real-Time Solution Suite to expand enterprise real-time data infrastructure.

Q3 FY2026 results: organic ASV grew 7.1% YoY to $2.48B, revenue rose 6.4% YoY to $622.9M, and adjusted EPS grew 6.1% to $4.53; included $19.6M of restructuring/severance costs. Management reaffirmed guidance; the 10-Q again disclosed the open IT general-controls material weakness.

Announced a strategic partnership with Google Cloud to embed Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform capabilities into the FactSet Workstation and jointly build AI agents for portfolio operations, deal advisory, and corporate finance workflows.

CFO Helen Shan announced she would transition out of the role effective April 13, 2026; Joshua Warren (former Envestnet CFO, prior BlackRock strategy roles) named successor. Company stated the change was unrelated to any accounting or financial-reporting disagreement.
Announced investment/partnership with Finster AI to help launch an AI-native banking solution built on FactSet data.

Shares rose ~6% on news of an integration letting users bring FactSet market data directly into Anthropic's Claude (via the Cowork enterprise connector), viewed as evidence FactSet's proprietary data could power next-generation AI applications rather than be disintermediated by them.

Stock fell to a 52-week low near $185 (down roughly 50-60% from 2025 highs of ~$387-450) amid an AI-disruption narrative; multiple sell-side downgrades/price-target cuts (e.g., Barclays Underweight, BofA initiated Underperform) cited fears that AI/LLM tools would erode the value of traditional financial terminal seats.
Leadership transition: Sanoke Viswanathan (former JPMorgan executive) became CEO, succeeding long-tenured CEO Phil Snow, who retired after roughly a decade in the role.

guidance.as_of: Investor Day, November 10, 2026 (reaffirming guidance first issued with Q4/FY2026 earnings on September 30, 2026)
guidance.fiscal_year: FY2027 (fiscal year ending August 31, 2027), with medium-term targets through FY2029

items.notes: A deceleration from the 7.1% organic ASV growth posted in Q4 FY2026; some analysts flagged this as a softer-than-hoped subscription growth guide.
Implies roughly 5-6% YoY total revenue growth off FY2026's $2.48B base.
Recovery from FY2026's ~28.3% GAAP operating margin as restructuring charges roll off.
Excludes $85M-$97M ($2.15-$2.25/diluted share) of intangible amortization and other discrete items.
Compares with FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $3.41 in Q4 alone / full-year GAAP EPS pressured by restructuring charges.
Implies roughly 7-9% growth versus FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS of $18.01.
Part of the financial algorithm unveiled November 10, 2026.
Implies continued margin expansion beyond the FY2027 range as restructuring and remediation costs fade and AI investment matures.
Supported by margin expansion and continued buybacks.
FY2026 free cash flow of $707.5M was already up 14.6% YoY.

guidance.management_commentary: At the November 10, 2026 Investor Day, management framed FY2026's restructuring and leadership changes as a reset that positions FactSet for accelerating, AI-enabled growth, reaffirming FY2027 guidance while laying out a longer-dated FY2029 algorithm (~6% organic revenue growth, 36%+ adjusted operating margin, ~10% adjusted EPS growth). On the Q4 FY2026 call, management emphasized that AI solutions ASV more than doubled year over year and that clients adopting FactSet's own AI tools are growing ASV meaningfully faster than the rest of the book, directly countering the AI-disruption bear thesis, while acknowledging the FY2027 organic ASV growth guide (5.0-6.5%) represents a step-down from the 7.1% exit rate as some one-time tailwinds normalize.

bull_case: AI is proving to be a net positive so far, not a disruptor: AI solutions ASV more than doubled in FY2026, and clients adopting FactSet's own AI tools are growing ASV meaningfully faster than the rest of the book — early evidence the AI-disruption bear case may be overstated, at least for FactSet's embedded-enterprise model.

Extremely sticky, long-duration client base (95%+ retention, 16+ year average tenure, multi-year enterprise agreements with no price compression) provides highly visible, recurring cash flows that are difficult for AI-native entrants to displace quickly given regulatory/compliance requirements for sourced, auditable data.

Valuation and sentiment have recovered materially from the 2026 AI-fear selloff (stock round-tripped from ~$185 lows back toward $330+), with the November Investor Day's FY2029 algorithm (6% organic growth, 36%+ margins, ~10% EPS CAGR) giving the market a multi-year roadmap for margin recovery once restructuring and remediation costs fade.

Partnerships with Google Cloud (Gemini agents), Anthropic (Claude data connector), Finster AI, and TIFIN.AI position FactSet as critical infrastructure — a trusted, auditable data layer — for AI agents in regulated finance, rather than being disintermediated by them.

Bolt-on M&A (BCC Group for real-time data, LiquidityBook for OMS, Irwin for IR) continues to expand FactSet's addressable workflow footprint, and free cash flow growth (+14.6% in FY2026 to $707.5M) funds both buybacks and a growing dividend ($1.16/quarter) even through a heavy investment year.
bear_case: The core AI-disruption thesis may still be right, just early: if LLM-based tools eventually commoditize basic data retrieval, screening, and analysis that historically justified premium workstation seat pricing, FactSet's per-seat/per-client economics could erode structurally even as near-term ASV metrics look healthy — the stock's 2026 round-trip shows how quickly this narrative can reprice the shares in either direction.

FY2027 organic ASV growth guidance (5.0-6.5%) is a deceleration from the 7.1% exit rate in Q4 FY2026, and GAAP operating margin fell ~390bps in FY2026 to ~28.3% on restructuring charges — raising the question of whether cost cuts and AI investment are translating into durable re-acceleration or just stabilizing a maturing business.

An unresolved IT general-controls material weakness, first disclosed in FY2024 and still open through recent filings, combined with a workforce reduction and simultaneous CEO (Sept 2025) and CFO (April 2026) transitions, signals elevated execution and financial-reporting risk at a company whose brand is built on data accuracy and trust.

FactSet remains the smaller player against Bloomberg (~33% share) and LSEG/Refinitiv (~20% share), both of which have more resources to invest in competing AI capabilities and greater data breadth, limiting FactSet's ability to win share in a technology arms race.

Growth remains modest in absolute terms (mid-single-digit-to-high-single-digit organic ASV growth) relative to a share price back near prior highs (~$330, within 5% of the 52-week high) and a consensus analyst view that has skewed toward Hold/Reduce ratings with price targets often below the current trading level — leaving less room for multiple expansion if FY2027 growth undershoots the low end of guidance.
